in the present study we have shown that in conditions similar with those imposed during the exercise‐in heat protocol, age and age related characteristics affect the overall heat gain rate as well as the efficiency of the mechanisms through which the body heat is being dissipation.
prepubertal children are more efficient than young adults and elderly men in dissipating heat, while elderly men are less efficient in dissipating heat than young adults and prepubertal subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thermoregulation during exercise in hot environments is a very complex phenomenon, and that the physiological and metabolic characteristics of an individual, as well as their interaction with the environment and exercise intensity, are important determinants of thermoregulation.

the age‐related differences in thermoregulatory efficiency are likely due to a combination of factors including differences in the magnitude of metabolic heat production and differences in the ability to lose heat via sweat.
the thermoregulation of young and elderly subjects is similar to each other, but different from that of prepubertal subjects.
